sections.text: Introduction
This document outlines the standard test method for hydrazine in water. The method covers the colorimetric determination of hydrazine in water.

This document initiated by Chemist Doaa Abd El Moneam Kasem & reviewed by 
 director Chemist Hoda Hasanen, revised by quality control Chemist: Mohamed 
 Mosbah Mokpel at EDEPCo, and approved by Eng: Awad M. Fatthy Head Sector of 
 Talkha PS, also reviewed by Chemist Yasen Abd-EL Menam Mohamed from CCL 
 and tested by Chemist Mohamed Amen Mohamed Mostafa from CCL and approved 
 by Chemist: Mohamed Abdel Hafez Head Sector of Central Chemical Laboratories.
Significance

Hydrazine is a man-made chemical and is not found in natural waters. The determination of hydrazine is usually made 
 on boiler feedwaters, process waters and other waters that have been treated with hydrazine ( N2H4 ) to prevent corrosion by dissolved oxygen.

This reducing chemical reacts with dissolved oxygen to form nitrogen and water. However, under certain conditions it can also decompose to form ammonia and nitrogen. Hydrazine is used extensively as a preboiler treatment chemical for high-pressure boiler to scavenge small amounts of dissolved oxygen, that are not removed by mechanical deaeration. It has the advantage over sulfite treatment in that it does not produce any dissolved solids in the boiler water. Hydrazine is often determined in concentrations below 0.1 mg / liter. However, in layup solutions for the protection of idle boilers, hydrazine may be present in concentrations as high as 200 mg / liter.
Additionally, hydrazine provides protection to carbon steel by chemically reducing the unprotective layers of ferric oxide ( Fe2O3 ) to a more adherent protective layer of magnetic ( Fe3O4 ).
Summary of Method

Para-dimethylaminobenzaldhyde produces a specific, yellow reaction product with hydrazine. The intensity of the yellow color is proportional to the amount of hydrazine in the water, and follows Beer's law.
Interferences

The substances normally present in industrial water dont interfere with the test; however, the hydrazine content may be diminished by oxidizing agents collected with the sample or absorbed by it prior to testing.
Colors in the prescribed wavelengths also interfere, as do other dark colors or turbidities that cannot be overcome by the prescribed treatment.
Safety Precautions

items:
The sample must be taken as the applicable ASTM methods D 
 3370-76.

The sample must be kept away from exposure to direct 
 sunlight.

Acids such 
 as Hydrochloric acid and others are dangerous, so you have to wear breathing 
 mask.

Keep this 
 acids closed. Do not get it in the eyes, on the skin, or on clothing. Do not 
 breathe them, use only in a hood.

sections.text: Tools and Equipment
Apparatus

Colorimeter- 
It is suitable for measurements at 425 nm or 458 nm. Certain 
photoelectric filter photometers are capable of measurements at 425 nm, but not 
at 458 nm. Measurements may be made at 425 nm, with a reduction in sensitivity 
of approximately 50 % of that possible at 458 nm.
Reagents

Purity of Reagents- 
 All reagents shall conform to the specification of the Committee on Analytical Reagents of the American Chemical Society, where such specification is available. Other grades may be used that the reagent is of sufficiently high purity to permit its use without lessening the accuracy of the determination.

Hydrazine, Standard Solution (1ml = 0.1 N2H4)
 Dissolve 0.328 g of hydrazine dihydrochloride ( N2H4 . 2HCl ) in 100 ml of water and 10 ml of HCl ( sp gr 1.19 ). Dilute 
 with water to 1 liter in a volumetric flask, and mix.

Hydrochloric Acid (sp gr 1.19 )
 Concentrated hydrochloric acid ( HCl ).

Hydrochloric Acid ( 1 + 9 )-
Mix 1 volume of HCl (sp gr 1.19) with 9 volume of water.

Hydrochloric Acid ( 1 + 99 )-
Mix 1 volume of HCl (sp gr 1.19) with 99 volume of water.

Para-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde Solution-
Dissolve 4.0 gm of para-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde in 200 ml of methyl alcohol 
( CH3OH) and 20 ml of HCl (sp.gr.1.19). Store in dark bottle out of direct sunlight.

Purity of Water-
Water shall be freshly boiled and free of dissolved oxygen.
Sampling

Analyze the sample as 
soon after collection as practicable, since hydrazine undergoes auto-oxidation 
as well as oxidation by oxidizing agents. Such agents may be in the sample or 
may enter the sample from the atmosphere.

If it is suspected 
that oxidation of the hydrazine in the sample is occurring in the interval 
between collection and analysis, or if the sample is not to be analyzed 
immediately, collect under acid. Place 5.0 ml of HCl (1+9) in a 50-ml volumetric 
flask, and collect sufficient sample in the flask to bring the total volume to 
50 ml.
Work to be Carried Out
Calibration

Prepare a series of hydrazine standards by making appropriate dilutions of the hydrazine solution (1ml = 0.1mg N2H4 ) with HCl 
( 1+99 ), so that a 50 ml aliquot of each dilution will contain the desired quantity of hydrazine( 0.2 to 5.0 g ) .

Pipette 50 ml 
portions of hydrazine standard solutions into 100 ml beakers, flasks, or cylinders and proceed as directed in the following procedure, except do not add more acid. Plot 
transmittance against micrograms of hydrazine.

A separate calibration curve must be made for each photometer and a recalibration must be made if it is necessary to change the cell, lamp, or filter, or if any alterations of instrument or reagents are made.Check the curve for each series of tests by running two or more solutions of known hydrazine concentrations.
Procedure

Add from a burette 
 exactly 5.0 ml of HCl (1+9) to a 100 ml beaker, flask, or cylinder, unless the sample was collected under acid, in which case, proceed directly as described in
 the next 
 step, except to use HCl (1+99) instead of water for diluting to 50 ml.

Transfer to the 100 
ml beaker, flask or cylinder a portion of the sample that will contain 
approximately 0.20 to 5.0 g of N2H4 by means of a 
graduated pipette. Add water from a graduated burette or pipette to make a final 
volume of exactly 50 ml, and mix. Add 10 ml of p-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde solution with a pipette, and mix. Let the mixture stand at least 10 min and not more than 100 min. Measure and compare the color by means of the colorimeter. Make Photometric measurements at approximately 458 nm.

Prepare a blank 
containing no added hydrazine in order to correct for color of the unreacted p-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde 
and any optical effects involved in adjusting the photometer for100 % 
transmission, in photometric procedures, with water showing no appreciable color.
